text:
Zeev Buium is 20, already an alternate captain in Vancouver, and playing 21 minutes a night on a team that is losing most of them. He has four assists and no goals in 19 games. The 12th pick of 2024 out of the University of Denver is roughly on the curve for defensemen picked 7th to 17th, whose median first full season was 0.24 points a game. He's at 0.21.

The five-on-five results are hard to look at: 36% of the expected goals with him on the ice, about six points worse than without him. Evolving-Hockey's numbers last season had opponents creating more against him than against 93% of defensemen, but also put his teammates in the bottom 7% by impact, and noted he draws more penalties than he takes.

The skills that got him drafted are visible. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking has him carrying the puck in on 46% of his entries, and his "plays like" list starts with Cam Fowler and Owen Power. Our range says 18 to 34 points over a full season. This is a development year on a bad team; judge him in March, not November.
headline: Buium's hard development year
